items.title: Introduction to Mission Control agent
items.summary: When an inference endpoint slows down, finding the cause usually means working through dashboards, metrics and deployment config by hand. CoreWeave Mission Control Agent is built into the CoreWeave Console. You describe the problem in plain language, the agent investigates your telemetry, and it can make the fix itself. In this demo, a GLM-5.2 endpoint is returning slow responses. The agent traces the problem to KV cache pressure, switches the model to NVFP4 weights, then splits it into two tensor-parallel replicas. Throughput goes up on the same eight GPUs, with no new hardware. What you'll see: - Asking questions in plain language from the CoreWeave Console, with no PromQL or dashboard digging - Investigation across CKS clusters, nodes, SUNK clusters and Slurm jobs, AI Object Storage, alerts, usage and CoreWeave docs - Answers built from your metrics, logs, dashboards and live resource state Inline charts, tables and resource cards generated from your own telemetry - Each tool call shown as a live step, so you can follow how it reached its answer - Actions on your infrastructure when you ask for them, such as updating an inference deployment Learn More: https://utm.io/us6TL

items.title: CoreWeave Sandboxes demo: RL, agent tool use, and model evaluation
items.summary: CoreWeave Sandboxes is an execution layer for reinforcement learning (RL), agent tool use, and model evaluation. Launched in public preview on May 14, 2026. In this 2-minute demo, Deok Filho, Product Manager at CoreWeave, walks through how CoreWeave Sandboxes works, the two consumption paths, and how researchers spin up thousands of sandboxes in parallel for RL rollouts and SWE-bench evaluations. Chapters 0:00 The sandbox problem in agentic AI 0:34 Introducing CoreWeave Sandboxes 0:38 Two paths: serverless vs. on-cluster 1:14 Setting up Profiles and the Runner 1:44 Using the Python SDK 1:58 Scaling sandboxes for RL and evaluations 2:18 Get started Frequently asked questions: What is CoreWeave Sandboxes? CoreWeave Sandboxes is an execution layer for AI workflows that need to run untrusted code in isolated environments. It supports reinforcement learning, agent tool use, and model evaluation at scale. How do I access CoreWeave Sandboxes? Two paths. Existing CoreWeave customers can enable sandboxes on their CKS cluster through the Cloud Console. Researchers without a CoreWeave cluster can access serverless sandboxes through Weights & Biases. What's the difference between the two paths? The CKS path runs sandboxes on your existing CoreWeave infrastructure using contracted capacity, with platform-controlled Profiles that define networking policies, namespace strategies, and resource limits. The serverless path through Weights & Biases runs sandboxes on CoreWeave-managed compute with no infrastructure setup — researchers authenticate with their W&B API key and start running sandboxes in minutes. What frameworks does CoreWeave Sandboxes support? The Python SDK works with reinforcement learning frameworks like veRL (where each rollout gets its own sandbox) and evaluation benchmarks like SWE-bench. Is GPU supported? Sandboxes on CKS can run on the compute defined by your Profile, including your cluster's GPU nodes. The serverless path launches with CPU sandboxes at public preview. items.title: RAG, Graph RAG & Agentic RAG: How AI Retrieves and Uses Information
items.summary: A language model does not know your internal documents, and it does not know what happened after it was trained. Retrieval is how you close that gap. Terms covered: - Information Retrieval: finding relevant content from a large collection in response to a query - RAG (Retrieval-Augmented Generation): retrieve relevant documents at the moment a question is asked, then generate a grounded answer from them - Graph RAG: uses a knowledge graph to retrieve, so the system navigates relationships between entities instead of matching keywords - Agentic RAG: treats retrieval as active reasoning. It rewrites queries, routes across sources, checks whether results are useful and retries when they are not. Standard RAG for direct queries. Graph RAG when relationships matter. items.title: 98% of Qwen - Bonsai 2
items.summary: Bonsai 2 from PrismML squeezes Qwen3.8 27B into a 6 GB file by retraining every weight to −1, 0 or +1, and PrismML claims it keeps 98% of the full model's performance. On short tasks it matched the full model in my tests. Then I gave it a real job in an agentic loop: build an ISS tracker on a 3D globe. The full Qwen model built a working tracker. Bonsai never wrote a line of the app. It ran the exact same search 114 times and got the same answer every time. Compression holds up for chat and quick coding help on a laptop. items.title: CoreWeave Arena: Serverless inference + serverless RL
items.summary: See how prompt engineering helps an open-source model get close to a frontier model's accuracy on CoreWeave Serverless Inference, at a fraction of the cost. Compares an open source Text2SQL agent against the closed source Opus model by testing prompt engineering techniques on CoreWeave Serverless Inference. Using the same prompt and logging results to Weave, the presenter evaluates GLM 5.2 versus Opus 4.5 on accuracy and cost, moving from naive prompts through short examples, Chain of Thought, Self Consistency, Task Decomposition, and Skills. Opus performs much better than GLM 5.2 on the naive prompt, but Chain of Thought reduces the accuracy gap to about 3 points while Opus costs about 9 times more. Self Consistency improves accuracy but widens the gap again and costs 3 attempts, and GLM approaches Opus on most techniques except the naive prompt, achieving similar results at about a tenth of the price.
